lines.label: Summary
lines.text: A giant Chain Chomp chained to a peg in Bob-omb Battlefield, close to a cell that holds the Power Star of "Behind Chain Chomp's Gate".

from.quote: A giant Chain Chomp
is located on Bob-omb Battlefield in Super Mario 64
It is attached to a peg near a cell with the Power Star of

lines.label: Weak points
lines.text: You cannot beat it, since Chain Chomps are almost entirely invincible, but a Bob-omb or a box stuns it for a moment.

from.quote: In Super Mario games, they are almost entirely invincible
A Bob-omb, a box, or a Yoshi's egg in the remake can stun Chain Chomp briefly.

lines.label: Tips
lines.text: It lunges at you when you are near and takes three wedges of health on contact. Ground-pound its post three times to free it, and it lunges into the nearby cell and clears the gate for the star.

from.quote: The Chain Chomp lunges at Mario if he is nearby, taking away three wedges of his health on contact.
The Chain Chomp can be freed by ground-pounding its post three times, required for it to lunge into the cell nearby and clear

lines.label: Summary
lines.text: A small ghost that follows you in the courtyard of Peach's Castle and in Big Boo's Haunt; touching one takes two wedges of health.

from.quote: Boos (also called Baby Boos) appear in Super Mario 64
Boos are encountered in the courtyard of Peach's Castle and in Big Boo's Haunt.
Boos take away two wedges of health on contact.

lines.label: Weak points
lines.text: A punch, a kick or a ground pound defeats it. When you look at one it turns partly see-through; otherwise it is solid and follows you.

from.quote: Boos are defeated from either a punch, a kick, a Pound the Ground attack
When Boos are looked at, they become partially visible, but are fully opaque otherwise and follow the player character.

lines.label: Tips
lines.text: Each Boo in the courtyard holds a yellow coin, and each one in Big Boo's Haunt holds a blue coin.

from.quote: The Boos in the courtyard hold a Yellow Coin each, and those in Big Boo's Haunt each have a Blue Coin

lines.label: Summary
lines.text: The giant ghost who owns Big Boo's Haunt and leads the Boos; he is the boss of "Go on a Ghost Hunt", "Ride Big Boo's Merry-Go-Round" and "Big Boo's Balcony", and a touch costs three wedges of health.

from.quote: acting as the Boos' leader
Big Boo makes his debut in Super Mario 64 as the owner of Big Boo's Haunt, being the boss of "Go on a Ghost Hunt", "Ride Big Boo's Merry-Go-Round", and "Big Boo's Balcony".
If this Boo attacks Mario, he loses three wedges of health.

lines.label: Weak points
lines.text: He can be hurt only while visible, by ground-pounding him from above or punching him from the side. Three hits defeat him, and he gets smaller and faster after each one.

from.quote: Big Boo can be attacked only when visible, so Mario has to attack this massive ghost by either ground-pounding him from above or punching him from the side. He takes three hits to defeat, becoming smaller and faster after each hit.

lines.label: Tips
lines.text: In the first two missions you must defeat several nearby Boos to make him appear; in "Big Boo's Balcony" he is already there. Like a normal Boo he disappears when looked at and shows again when you turn away, and if you leave the area before he is beaten his health resets. / A Big Boo about twice the size of the other Boos waits in a corner of the castle courtyard, and beating it drops a birdcage that leads to Big Boo's Haunt.

from.quote: For the first two missions, Mario needs to defeat several nearby Boos to make him appear, though for the last one, he is automatically present
Like with the normal Boos, Big Boo disappears when looked at and becomes visible again when Mario turns away.
if the player leaves the area before completely defeating Big Boo, his health resets.
In the courtyard itself, it can be found in one of the corners, appearing about twice as large as the other Boos. If Mario defeats it, it drops a birdcage
leading to Big Boo's Haunt.

lines.label: Summary
lines.text: A sleepy plant with green lips, found in Whomp's Fortress in the original game, that is always asleep, with a lullaby playing, until you disturb it.

from.quote: They are depicted with green lips in the original version
Piranha Plants appear only in Whomp's Fortress
Piranha Plants have a sleepy nature, which is why they are always found asleep; during this, a lullaby plays.

lines.label: Weak points
lines.text: Walk up slowly and it stays asleep; touch it or rush at it and it wakes and bites toward you.

from.quote: When a Piranha Plant is either touched or approached quickly by the player character, it wakes up and starts to bite in the direction of the player character, though they stay asleep if approached slowly.

lines.label: Tips
lines.text: A bite takes three points of health, or four if you have lost your cap. A defeated Piranha Plant leaves a blue coin.

from.quote: Piranha Plants take away three health points if they bite the player character, or four if he is without his cap
Defeating certain enemies causes a Blue Coin to appear, including Koopa Troopas, Piranha Plants, Boos

lines.label: Summary
lines.text: A common walking bomb that first appears in Bob-omb Battlefield: when it spots you it lights its fuse and rushes at you.

from.quote: Bob-ombs are common enemies in Super Mario 64 and its Nintendo DS version. They first appear on the Bob-omb Battlefield.
When a Bob-omb spots the player, it lights its fuse and then rushes towards them from behind, attempting to damage them when it explodes.

lines.label: Weak points
lines.text: Touching one does no harm, but its explosion costs two wedges of health. Kick it, or pick it up from behind and throw it, and it explodes away from you and leaves a coin.

from.quote: Unlike in the Super Mario Bros. subseries, Bob-ombs do not harm the player upon contact. Their explosion, however, damages the player by two wedges of health.
Bob-ombs can be defeated by being kicked or picked up from behind and thrown. This causes them to explode away from the player, leaving behind a coin.

lines.label: Tips
lines.text: Their blasts also hurt other enemies nearby, and they come back after you leave the area. / A Bob-omb working a cannon does not chase you but still explodes if picked up; the pink Bob-omb Buddies are friendly, give hints and open cannons.

from.quote: Explosions caused by the bombs can also damage other enemies within the blast.
After the player character walks away from the area, the Bob-ombs then respawn.
These Bob-ombs do not chase the player, but they still explode if picked up.
Bob-omb Buddies are friendly and give the player character helpful hints. They open cannons
